name: Dusky Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Mountains of central mexico (michoacán to oaxaca)
description: Rather drab, “female-plumaged,” medium-size hummingbird of arid scrubby habitats, including gardens and open woodlands. Feeds at all levels and usually wags and fans tail persistently while hovering—a good field character.

name: Indian Nuthatch
rangeDescription: Foothills of northern and central india (western ghats)
description: Only nuthatch in most of its range with gray upperparts and brick-red underparts. From crown to upper mantle, the gray is a lighter shade than the remainder of the upperparts.

name: European Honey-buzzard
rangeDescription: Western palearctic; winters southern europe and iran to southern africa
description: Lanky raptor with a slender head and long wings with prominent “fingers.” Plumage is highly variable, but note tail pattern: pale overall with a dark tip, and two wide-spaced narrow dark bars on the basal half. Compare with the much stockier Common Buzzard, which has a shorter neck, more rounded wings, and steadier wingbeats.

name: Mantled Hawk
rangeDescription: Tropical forest of eastern brazil to eastern uruguay and eastern paraguay
description: Largish hawk with a short tail and very broad wings. White head, belly and tail with a barred black back.

name: Colorful Puffleg
rangeDescription: West slope of western andes of colombia (cauca)
description: Rare hummingbird known only from a tiny area of Colombia’s western Andes west of Popayán. Adult male is iridescent green with a blue belly, red vent, and white leg puffs.

name: Orange-throated Sunangel
rangeDescription: Andes of northeastern colombia to northwestern venezuela (southern lara to táchira)
description: Medium-sized hummingbird with a short, straight bill found in the Andes of Venezuela and eastern Colombia. Male has a green body, buff and green spotted underparts, and a glittering orange throat.

name: Crested Hornero
rangeDescription: Chaco of southeastern bolivia to western paraguay and northern argentina
description: A mostly terrestrial and chunky light brown bird of the north and central Chaco, from central Argentina to Western Paraguay and extreme SE Bolivia. Distinguished from Rufous Hornero by crest, from Lark-like Brushrunner by plain plumage, and from Cachalotes by dull plumage, smaller bill and size, and dark iris.

name: Daurian Starling
rangeDescription: Southeastern siberia to northern mongolia and northern korea; winters to southeastern asia
description: Small, strongly migratory starling; common on its wintering grounds, but localized when breeding, and often difficult to find when on migration. Male dark above, white below, but intricately patterned, with shades of violet, green, and orange in wings.

name: Rusty-throated Parrotbill
rangeDescription: Mountains of south-central china (southeastern qinghai to southeastern gansu and adjacent sichuan)
description: A distinctive mid-sized parrotbill with a highly restricted range; limited to a small part of central China where it inhabits mid- to high-altitude montane scrub and open forests with dense low cover, particularly bamboo stands. Dull brown with a gray head, long black eyebrow, and a dark rusty-red face and throat.

name: Chestnut-bellied Cotinga
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of ecuador and far northern peru
description: Rare bird of stunted treeline forest in the high Andes of Ecuador and southern Colombia. Mostly gray with a chestnut belly; male has a black cap.

name: Braun's Bushshrike
rangeDescription: Northwestern angola (cuanza norte escarpment)
description: A striking, mostly blackish bushshrike with a bright orange throat and breast, a chestnut crown and nape, and a white belly and wing-stripe. Pairs are scarce and skulky in the understory of secondary and gallery forest at only six localities near Uige along the Angolan escarpment, between 600 and 1260 meters of elevation.

name: Palawan Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Lowlands of palawan (southwestern philippines)
description: A small bird of lowland and foothill forest on Palawan. Favors undergrowth with palms or bamboo.

name: Mariana Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Mariana islands (saipan, tinian, agiguan, rota, and guam)
description: A spectacularly colorful dove with a bright green body, an orange belly, a dark chest band, a bright silver neck and chest, a slim white eyebrow, and a striking magenta forehead. Wings have dark splodges on them.

name: Subtropical Doradito
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to northwestern argentina (south to la rioja)
description: A bright flycatcher found in marshes in the Andes from Colombia to Argentina. Yellow below and olive above, sometimes showing a hint of a dark mask and dull yellowish edges on the wing feathers.

name: Royal Penguin
rangeDescription: Macquarie island and adjacent islets
description: The largest crested penguin, with a diagnostic whitish face. Only breeds on the Australian-administered Macquarie Island; occasionally seen off of New Zealand’s subantarctic islands, rarely off of the mainland.

name: Maroon Pigeon
rangeDescription: Forest of são tomé (gulf of guinea)
description: A large, very dark pigeon with a grayish head, a burgundy body with scattered small white spots, and a bright yellow bill and legs. Female is duller than the male.

name: Ranongga White-eye
rangeDescription: Forest of ranongga (west-central solomon islands)
description: Small. Olive-green above and banana-yellow below and on throat.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Wire-crested Thorntail
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to eastern ecuador and northeastern peru
description: Small, compact hummingbird found on the east slope of Andes from central Colombia to central Peru. Male is unmistakable; look for long pointed tail, wirelike crest, short straight bill, and white band across the rump.

name: Grauer's Broadbill
rangeDescription: Itombwe mountains of eastern democratic republic of the congo and southwestern uganda
description: A unique dumpy green flycatcher-like broadbill with a buffy crown, a black eye-stripe, and a powder-blue throat and vent. Juvenile duller.

name: Bannerman's Turaco
rangeDescription: Southwestern cameroon (bamenda-banso highlands)
description: A long-tailed, bulky greenish turaco with a yellow bill, a red crest, and gray cheeks. In flight, it explodes from the canopy, showing distinctive deep red panels in the wings.
